allNodeData.name: Bases and Dirac
allNodeData.description:
When considering continuous spectra, we can think of $\Psi(x,t)$ itself as the components of the abstract vector in hilbert space $\ket{S(t)}$ describing our state. That is:

$\Psi(x,t)=\braket{x|S(t)}$ with

$\ket{S(t)}=\int_{-\infty}^\infty \Psi(x,t)\ket{x}$ (exploiting orthogonality)

Note here that $x$ in the wavefunction is a spatial location, $\bra{x}$ is the position eigenstate which has an associated eigenvalue of the same $x$ that was input into the wavefunction. i.e. we are finding the value of the wavefunction at $x_0$ by projecting the abstract state of the system at time t, $S(t)$, onto the eigenstate $\ket{x_0}$. Which in the case of the position operator, is a dirac delta centered on $x_0$.

Consider the identity operator:

$\sum\limits_n\ket{e_n}\bra{e_n}=1$

If it acted on some ket $\ket{\alpha}$ we get:

$\sum\limits_n(\braket{e_n|\alpha})\ket{\alpha}=\ket{\alpha}$

That is, we get the components of any vector in our basis $\{\ket{e_n}\}$

allNodeData.name: Parallel Axis Theorem
allNodeData.description:
The moment of inertia about an axis parallel to one going through the center of a body is equal to:

$Mh^2+I_{cm}$ 

where $I_{cm}$ is the moment of inertia through the body's center of mass and $h$ is the distance between the 2 axes.
